question: A cyclist rides 10 km at an average speed of 15 km/hr and then the next 15 km at an average speed of 10 km/hr. The average speed of the entire ride is:
solution:
**Given:**

A cyclist rides 10 km at an average speed of 15 km/hr and then the next 15 km at an average speed of 10 km/hr.

**Formula used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

**Calculation:**

First part:

Distance₁ = 10 km

Speed₁ = 15 km/hr

Time₁ = Distance₁ / Speed₁

⇒ Time₁ = 10 / 15

⇒ Time₁ = 2/3 hr

Second part:

Distance₂ = 15 km

Speed₂ = 10 km/hr

Time₂ = Distance₂ / Speed₂

⇒ Time₂ = 15 / 10

⇒ Time₂ = 1.5 hr

Total Distance = Distance₁ + Distance₂

⇒ Total Distance = 10 + 15

⇒ Total Distance = 25 km

Total Time = Time₁ + Time₂

⇒ Total Time = 2/3 + 1.5

⇒ Total Time = 2/3 + 3/2

⇒ Total Time = 4/6 + 9/6

⇒ Total Time = 13/6 hr

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 25 / (13/6)

⇒ Average Speed = 25 × 6/13

⇒ Average Speed = 150/13

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 11.54 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**
